newsitem.title: INDIA: India needs $55.9 mln investment to revamp ports.
newsitem.headline: India needs $55.9 mln investment to revamp ports.

text.p: India must invest two billion rupees ($55.9 million) to develop and upgrade its smaller ports over the next five years, Surface Transport Minister T.G. Venkatraman has said.

"The government of India has projected a demand of two billion rupees in the ninth plan for development of minor ports in the country," Venkatraman said in a statement issued late on Thursday. The ninth plan covers 1997 to 2002.
India has courted foreign and private investment to spruce up its infrastructure facilities as part of an economic reform programme that began in 1991.
The productivity of the ports grew by seven to 10 percent over the last five years despite the capacity constraints, the Transport Ministry statement said.
The foreign exchange savings of the shipping industry as a whole had risen to 32.12 billion rupees during 1995/96 from 26.53 billion in the previous year, he said.
The statement said clear and transparent guidelines for private sector investments had been issued last month to expedite investments in the port sector.

The government is also proposing to involve the private sector in developing about 4,000 km (2,500 miles) of high density four-lane highways, 40 bridges, 30 by-passes and several rail over bridges, the minister said.
